newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TRUCKERS' STRIKE COULD END FRIDAY -- UNION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TRUCKERS' STRIKE COULD END FRIDAY -- UNION.

text.p: South African union and employer negotiators signalled on Thursday night that an agreement could be reached within a day on the nationwide wage strike by at least 30,000 truckers.

Transport and General Workers' Union national organiser Thulani Dlamini said after more than four hours of mediation that both workers and employers were assessing an offer and would meet again at 1200 GMT on Friday.
"It's very acceptable, fair and balanced for both sides. I think it's a package that can't be refused by either party," he told Reuters.

Dlamini declined to disclose the figures in the package, saying negotiations were at a sensitive and critical stage. However, he said union officials believed their members would end the strike and return to work.
"We're confident that we will get a mandate to sign," he said. "We'll get workers rushing to work because it's so nice."
Road Freight Employers' Association chairman Johan van der Walt was more cautious but also said a deal could be struck.
"A lot of progress has been made -- we might have a deal in the making... I'm fairly optimistic," van der Walt told Reuters.
The mediation was chaired by the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA), a vehicle for dispute resolution which provides statutory dispute resolution services.
The strike started Wednesday morning and has so far taken the form of pickets at trucking companies which have resorted to employing scab labour.
It is the first strike in the sector in 50 years and also the first nationwide strike under the New Labour Relations Act which came into effect earlier this month.
The average wage for truckers is 321 rand per week for general workers in the bigger centres of South Africa.
